'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kramatorsk restaurant attack]]
****A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strike on a restaurant in [[Kramatorsk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], kills 13 [[civilian]]s and injures 61 others. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jun/27/deadly-russian-missile-strike-on-busy-pizza-restaurant-in-kramatorsk (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/ukraine-war-russia-kramatorsk-putin-b2365996.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Wagner Group rebellion]]
***[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] confirms that the head of the [[Wagner Group]], [[Yevgeny Prigozhin]], has arrived in [[Belarus]] in accordance with the agreement reached with the [[Russian government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-pays-tribute-russian-pilots-killed-fighting-mutineers-2023-06-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
***Suspected [[jihadist]]s kill several [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|Burkinabé soldiers]] and members of the [[Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland|Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland]] in a series of attacks on troops in the village of Noaka, [[Pissila Department|Pissila department]], [[Sanmatenga Province]], and in the [[Sahel Region]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/burkina-troops-allied-militiamen-killed-in-attacks-security-sources-say/7155308.html (AFP via VOA)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Austrians|Austrian]] painter [[Gustav Klimt]]'s last completed [[oil painting]], ''[[Lady with a Fan (Klimt)|Lady with a Fan]]'', sets a new [[Art of Europe|European]] [[art auction]] record when an unnamed [[art dealer]] buys it for [[Pound sterling|£]]85.3 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]108.4M), including the [[buyer's premium]], at [[Sotheby's]] in [[London]], UK. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/klimts-last-portrait-sets-european-record-in-127m-auction (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*One person is injured and many buildings are damaged after a magnitude 5.1 [[List of earthquakes in Ecuador|earthquake]] strikes [[Muisne]], [[Esmeraldas Province|Esmeraldas]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://www.eluniverso.com/noticias/ecuador/danos-por-sismo-de-55-en-muisne-nota/ (''El Universo'')]
* At least four people are killed when landslides caused by flash floods hit [[Wenchuan County]], [[Sichuan]], [[China]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-landslides-wenchuan-flash-floods-e10085106c59c475721baa2f945a9190 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023 Canadian wildfires]]
**Smoke from the [[wildfire]]s continues to blanket [[southern Ontario]] and the [[Eastern United States|eastern]] and [[mid-western United States]], including [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Michigan]], [[Illinois]], [[Ohio]], [[Indiana]] and [[Kentucky]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/amphtml/midwest-air-quality-canada-wildfire-smoke-chicago-wisconsin-grand-rapids-172026191.html (Yahoo! News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*''[[Moore v. Harper]]''
**In a 6–3 decision, the [[Supreme Court of the United States|U.S. Supreme Court]] rules that the [[Elections Clause]] does not give state legislatures sole power over elections, rejecting the [[independent state legislature theory|theory of independent state legislatures]]. [https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-elections-state-legislatures-a620db8c1ad30fc34b3ab0c81b29b87c (AP)]
*[[Killing of Nahel Merzouk]]
**A 17-year-old boy is shot dead by a [[National Police (France)|police officer]] after an attempted [[traffic stop]] in [[Nanterre]], [[Hauts-de-Seine]], [[Île-de-France]]. [https://amp.france24.com/en/live-news/20230627-probe-after-french-police-kill-teenaged-driver-who-refused-to-stop (France 24)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Fourteen [[Law enforcement in Mexico|police]] employees are [[kidnap]]ped by armed men in [[Chiapas]], [[Mexico]], while travelling on the [[Mexican Federal Highway 190|190 motorway]] between [[Ocozocoautla]] and [[Tuxtla Gutiérrez]]. [https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/latest-news/14-police-employees-kidnapped-in-mexico-officials/ (AFP via ''Jamaica Observer'')]
*One [[park ranger]] is killed and another is injured in an attack by armed men near an [[Illegal mining|illegal mine]] at the [[Okapi Wildlife Reserve]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/01/world/clash-at-dr-congo-wildlife-reserve-leaves-ranger-dead/1898504 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Sierra Leonean general election]]
**[[Julius Maada Bio]] is sworn in as [[president of Sierra Leone]] for a second consecutive term. His opponent, former [[Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Sierra Leone)|Foreign Minister]] [[Samura Kamara]], rejects the results and claims [[electoral fraud|the election was rigged]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/06/27/africa/maada-bio-reelected-sierra-leone-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*The [[National Assembly (Republika Srpska)|National Assembly]] of [[Republika Srpska]] votes to suspend all decisions of [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]]'s [[Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Constitutional Court]], a move described as "legal secession" and a violation of the 1995 [[Dayton Agreement]]. The region's [[President of Republika Srpska|president]], [[Milorad Dodik]], had criticised the court for having foreign judges and an [[Anti-Serb sentiment|anti-Serb]] bias. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/bosnian-serb-lawmakers-vote-suspend-rulings-bosnias-top-court-2023-06-27/ (Reuters)]
